hazards.control: Pressure test before opening to the well; bleed down and verify zero before breaking any connection.
Stay clear of the coil path, the gooseneck, and flowback iron under flow.
Certified lifting gear; no one under the injector while it is suspended.
Hands clear of the injector chains, the reel, and the stripper door.

name: Coiled tubing pressure control stack and injector
function: The assembly on the tree during a drillout: hands-free bottom adapter, quad BOP, riser, side-door stripper, injector head with its chains and motors, and the gooseneck that guides the coil from the reel into the injector.

tabs.overview: Bottom to top: the bottom adapter lands on the tree top adapter; the quad BOP carries pipe, slip, shear, and blind rams; the riser gives room for the BHA above the rams; the stripper seals around the moving coil; the injector head grips the coil between two chains fitted with gripper blocks, driven by hydraulic motors, and the load cell under it reads weight; the gooseneck bends the coil from the reel over into the injector on rollers. Use the section and translucent tools to follow the coil down through the stack.
tabs.engineering: Rated to the wellhead pressure at the BOP; the riser length is set by the longest BHA; the injector pull and snub ratings are matched to the coil and the expected pressure. Hydraulic supply from the power pack; all functions run from the control cabin.
tabs.connections: Tree top adapter below; kill and equalizing ports on the BOP; coil to the reel through the gooseneck; hydraulic lines to the power pack.
tabs.safety: Barrier philosophy: stripper while moving, pipe rams when stopped, shear and blind for an emergency; stack tested before the swab valve is opened.
tabs.evidence: Public coiled tubing pressure control guide (S24), API RP 16ST and API RP 5C7 scope (S23, S26), field practice (S9).
tabs.operations: Assembled on the ground, tested, lifted onto the tree as one piece by the crane or mast.
tabs.failure_modes: Stripper element wear, ram seal leaks, chain and gripper wear, gooseneck roller damage, hydraulic leaks.
